evidence: Cic. Att. 11.6.2: nōn nōminātim sed generātim (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 3.65: nisi nōminātim dictum esset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “by name”: naming persons or things one by one, as opposed to generātim, “in general”. In Plautus also “one by one, in detail” (Lewis & Short).
Of what is stated outright, “clearly, distinctly”. From disertus, eloquent, and so it also means “eloquently” (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sen. Ep. 7.1: quid tibi vītandum praecipuē exīstimēs quaeris?
terms.comment: For “specifically” in the sense “in particular”; see particular and especially.

phrases.latin: quicquid esset in praediō vitiī, id statuērunt, sī vēnditor scīret, nisi nōminātim dictum esset, praestārī oportēre
phrases.english: they ruled that any defect in a property that the seller knew of must be made good, unless it had been specifically declared

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
